MUJAHID:v2p729/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p729/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p729/r1.claim: Mujahid says the reminder is mention of the Hour.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p347/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p347/r1.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p347/r1.claim: Urwa ibn al-Zubayr says the Prophet kept asking about the Hour until this verse descended, after which he stopped asking.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p513#9/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p513#9/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p513#9/r1.claim: The Prophet has no knowledge of the Hour's timing.

TAB-FULL:v24p100/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p100/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p100/r2.claim: The Prophet has no assigned role in determining the Hour or investigating its timing; its endpoint belongs to God.

TAB-FULL:v24p100/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p100/r3.speaker: عائشة
TAB-FULL:v24p100/r3.claim: ʿĀʾisha says people kept asking the Prophet about the Hour until the verse was revealed.

TAB-FULL:v24p100/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p100/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p100/r5.claim: Mujāhid says “its remembrance” means the Hour.

NAHHAS:v5p146/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p146/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p146/r12.claim: The Prophet is not responsible for the Hour's date because he does not know it; mā loses alif to distinguish question from statement, and stopping without written hāʾ is incorrect.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r11.claim: The question means: why do the polytheists ask you about the Hour when you do not know it?

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r12.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r12.claim: It may mean why Muhammad asks about the Hour when he has no right to ask about it.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p202#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p202#2/r1.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p202#2/r1.claim: He explains the question as saying that God has not disclosed knowledge of the Hour to the Prophet.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p202#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p202#2/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p202#2/r2.claim: He paraphrases it as saying that the Prophet has no business speaking about the Hour.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p202#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p202#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p202#2/r3.claim: The meaning is that the Prophet has no knowledge or information about the Hour; the interrogative phrase conveys denial.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r8.claim: The Prophet has no knowledge of the Hour; the endpoint of its knowledge belongs to God.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p699/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p699/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p699/r2.claim: One reading asks what place the Prophet occupies in telling them its time; Aisha reports that he kept mentioning and asking about the Hour until this verse descended, expressing wonder at his concern.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p699/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p699/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p699/r3.claim: Alternatively, the question rebukes their asking: the Prophet's sending as the final messenger is itself a sign of the Hour's nearness and a reason to prepare, so asking its date is pointless.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r12.claim: The rebuke means the Prophet has no role in specifying the Hour; his task is only to warn those who fear it.

TABRISI:79:45-46/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:45-46/r10.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:79:45-46/r10.claim: Hasan says the Prophet knows the Hour will certainly happen but does not know its time.

TABRISI:79:45-46/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:45-46/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:45-46/r11.claim: Other views take the reply to mean that knowledge of the Hour is unrelated to the Prophet's mission as a caller, or that it quotes the questioners' impatience.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#9/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#9/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#9/r1.claim: The Prophet has no knowledge of the Hour; he does not know when it will occur.

RAZI-FULL:v31p48/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p48/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p48/r4.claim: One reading asks why the Prophet is occupied with remembering and disclosing its appointed time; Aisha reports that he kept mentioning and being asked about the Hour until this verse came down.

RAZI-FULL:v31p48/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p48/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p48/r5.claim: Another reading rebukes the question itself: the Prophet, final messenger, has given signs of the Hour's nearness, enough to prepare people, while its knowledge belongs to God alone.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r10.speaker: الزهري عن عروة بن الزبير
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r10.claim: The Prophet's frequent questioning is answered by saying the Hour's knowledge ends with God, so he is told not to seek it.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r11.claim: Alternatively, the question rebukes the polytheists: why ask Muhammad for details when he is not among those who know them? Ibn Abbas transmitted this sense.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r12.claim: Al-dhikrā here means remembrance or mention.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r2.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r2.claim: He says the Prophet kept being asked about the Hour until these verses were revealed.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r9.claim: The address asks Muhammad what place he has in reminding people about the Resurrection and questioning its time; he is not tasked to ask about it.

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:41-45/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:41-45/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:41-45/r3.claim: فيم أنت من ذكراها may deny the Prophet’s role in giving its time, since only God knows it and reminders deepen their error; or it calls him a sign of the Hour as the final prophet; another reading connects it directly to their question.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#4/r1.claim: “What are you in relation to its remembrance?” asks how he could tell or explain its time; the Prophet repeatedly mentioned it and asked about it, so the question expresses surprise at his concern.

QASHANI:79:34-41/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:79:34-41/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:79:34-41/r6.claim: Knowledge of the Hour ends with God: knowing it requires the annihilation of one’s knowledge in divine knowledge and one’s self in God’s Self.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p402/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p402/r4.speaker: عائشة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p402/r4.claim: Aisha says the Prophet was often asked about the Hour until this verse was revealed.

SAMIN-DURR:79:43/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:43/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:79:43/r1.claim: ‘Fima’ is a fronted predicate, ‘anta’ the delayed subject, and ‘min dhikraha’ attaches to the predicate; the meaning asks what role the Prophet has in reminding them and explaining its time.

SAMIN-DURR:79:43/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:43/r2.speaker: عائشة
SAMIN-DURR:79:43/r2.claim: A report from ‘A’isha says the Prophet repeatedly mentioned the Hour and asked about it until this verse was revealed.

SAMIN-DURR:79:43/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:43/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:79:43/r3.claim: On ‘A’isha’s report, al-Zamakhshari reads the verse as expressing wonder at the Prophet’s frequent preoccupation with remembering and asking about the Hour.

SAMIN-DURR:79:43/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:43/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:79:43/r4.claim: A second analysis pauses after ‘fima’: ‘what is this question?’ Then the Prophet’s sending as the final messenger is itself a sign of the Hour’s nearness, so asking its date is pointless.

SAMIN-DURR:79:43/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:43/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:79:43/r5.claim: The author calls that second analysis elegant but rejects it because it departs from the apparent construction and breaks the sentence’s order.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.claim: The surah’s purpose is to establish resurrection and the gathering, displaying humanity’s final fate after the preceding surahs’ full exposition; its oaths show the matter has reached its decisive climax.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r2.claim: The rebuke asks why the Prophet is expected to know its timing; even an answer would not help, though his compassion for their conversion might make him wish to reply.

DURR-FULL:v8p412/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p412/r11.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p412/r11.claim: Mujahid says the great calamity is when people are sent to Malik, guardian of Hell; ṭaghā means disobeyed, marsāhā means its time, and its mention means the Hour.

DURR-FULL:v8p412/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p412/r12.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v8p412/r12.claim: Ali says people asked the Prophet about the Hour, then the verse asked what he had to do with its mention.

BURSEVI:v10p255#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p255#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p255#2/r5.claim: “What are you concerned with its mention?” rejects their request: the Prophet cannot tell them its time because that knowledge belongs exclusively to God.

BURSEVI:v10p255#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p255#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p255#2/r6.claim: The verse’s implied sense is that the Prophet has no knowledge of its time to explain to them; even the question’s premise that he could disclose it is denied.

BURSEVI:v10p256/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p256/r2.speaker: القاشاني
BURSEVI:v10p256/r2.claim: Al-Qashani says knowing the Hour requires first effacing one’s own knowledge and then one’s self in God; the annihilated person has neither separate knowledge nor self to know it.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p37#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p37#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p37#2/r1.claim: The question rebukes the idolaters for asking the Prophet to specify the Hour's time; he has no role in teaching its date, as in 7:187.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p37#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p37#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p37#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, the first clause rejects their question and the next explains: the Prophet's sending as the final prophet is itself a sign that the Hour is near, enough knowledge for them.

ELMALILI:79:42-46/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:42-46/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:42-46/r2.claim: One reading rejects the question: the Prophet has no task of specifying the Hour and its timing lies beyond him.

ELMALILI:79:42-46/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:42-46/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:42-46/r3.claim: Another reading treats the question as misplaced and the Prophet's mission as itself a sign that the Hour is approaching; seeking further details exceeds their authority.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p95/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p95/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p95/r1.claim: The reply redirects their demand for a date toward what matters: the Prophet's task is to warn those who fear the Hour, a ‘wise style’ like the Prophet asking a questioner what he had prepared.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p95/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p95/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p95/r2.claim: A report in an authentic collection says that when a man asked the Prophet about the Hour, he asked what the man had prepared for it.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p95/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p95/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p95/r3.claim: Although addressed to the Prophet, the response is meant for the disbelievers to hear, and its separation from the question marks it as an answer.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p95/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p95/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p95/r4.claim: The interrogative ‘what’ expresses astonishment at and rebuke of their question.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p95/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p95/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p95/r5.claim: The preposition ‘in’ figuratively depicts them as surrounding the Prophet with questions about the Hour, as if he were occupied with knowledge of its date.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p95/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p95/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p95/r6.claim: The alif of ma is dropped after the preposition, as in the opening of al-Naba; fima is the fronted predicate and anta its subject.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p95/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p95/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p95/r7.claim: Min may explain the interrogative's ambiguity as ‘something that is its reminder,’ or describe a relation: the Prophet has no involvement with determining the Hour's time.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p96/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p96/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p96/r1.claim: Fronting fima emphasizes that the Prophet's involvement in the Hour's remembrance is what the question rebukes.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p96/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p96/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p96/r2.claim: Dhikra is a verbal noun meaning spoken remembrance in this context.

TABATABAI:79:42-44/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:42-44/r3.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:79:42-44/r3.claim: Raghib says dhikrā means frequent remembrance and is more emphatic than dhikr; the construction asks what knowledge the Prophet could gain from repeatedly mentioning the Hour.

TABATABAI:79:42-44/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:42-44/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:42-44/r4.claim: Alternatively, dhikrā is the heart's apprehension of a thing's true nature; the Prophet cannot know the Hour's reality and timing by frequent remembrance, which better fits the context.

TABATABAI:79:42-44/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:42-44/r5.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:79:42-44/r5.claim: Some say the Hour's remembrance is unrelated to the Prophet's mission, which is to warn those who fear it; another says the question is rebuked because his mission is already linked to the Hour and cites a report that he and the Hour were sent close together. The author finds these readings contextually weak and strained.

TABATABAI:79:42-44/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:42-44/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:79:42-44/r6.claim: Another view takes the phrase as part of the polytheists' question about what the Prophet knows from remembering the Hour; the author says the context does not suit it.

TABATABAI:79:46#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r6.speaker: عائشة
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r6.claim: A report graded sound by al-Hakim says the Prophet was repeatedly asked about the Hour until these verses were revealed, after which he was not asked; the author says the context does not fit this as a reply to the Prophet's own question.

ASAD-NOTES:79:42#n17/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:79:42#n17/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:79:42#n17/r1.claim: The phrase min dhikraha literally asks what relation the Prophet has to stating the Hour.

BINTSHATI:v1p160/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p160/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p160/r1.claim: The Qur’an deliberately redirects questions about the Hour’s time and place because God alone knows it; fronting the phrase restricts its endpoint to Him.

BINTSHATI:v1p160/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p160/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p160/r2.claim: God alone knows the Hour, and to Him alone it returns; its knowledge has not been granted to any created being.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:42/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:42/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:42/r3.claim: God's question means the Prophet cannot obtain this knowledge, which belongs to God alone (cf. Luqman 31:34).

QIRAAT-ER:79:43:1#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:79:43:1#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:79:43:1#1/r1.claim: In pause, hāʾ al-sakt yields fīmah; in continuation it is fīma, with the same interrogative construction.

STUDYQURAN:79:43/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:43/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:79:43/r1.claim: One reading has God tell the Prophet not to speak about what he does not know.

STUDYQURAN:79:43/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:43/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:79:43/r2.claim: Another reading answers people who argued the Prophet had no business mentioning the Hour and its signs without knowing their timing.

STUDYQURAN:79:43/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:43/r3.speaker: ʿĀʾishah
STUDYQURAN:79:43/r3.claim: A report says the Prophet wanted to ask when the Hour would come, but God told him he had no right to know.
